title: KMS Rotation & Fallback Handoff - Postmortem Review
summary: Quick postmortem of the Dec 29 KMS rotation-induced fallback where Verdant Labs experienced 30s spikes and partial decryption failures for private deployments. We reviewed root cause (staggered rotation + vault client TTL mismatch), agreed short-term mitigations (controlled rollback, increased circuit-breaker tolerance, audit log bundle), and mapped long-term hardening (HSM-backed rotation tests, canary rotations, improved observability). Explicit handoff of docs and runbooks to Verdant Ops and scheduling of a joint dry-run in staging.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM); Elena Morales (CISO, Verdant), Ben Chu (SRE), Ravi Kapoor (Platform Lead), Sana Iqbal (Ops)

-- Auto summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete) --
Verdant saw decryption/device failures during key rotation on Dec 29; fallback triggered to hosted key proxy which caused token latencies and partial errors. Discussed TTL mismatch between Vault client and rotate window, and a subsequent slow fallthrough to the Redwood fallback path.

[00:00] Jordan Hayes: hey everyone thanks for joining, we know folks are busy, we'll try to be tight. this is the postmortem + handoff on the kms rotation blip on december twenty ninth, is that right elena?
[00:08] Elena Morales: yes, thanks. we want the exact timeline, and, like, confirmation that the fallback won't leak any pii, and we need the audit evidence for compliance.
[00:18] Priya Nair: quick intro — priya, se on the infra team. i'll walk through observed traces and mitigation steps. Marcus is on for handoff notes.
[00:25] Ben Chu: real quick, we had a cascade — some requests saw 20 to 40 second tails, a subset failed crypto ops, and then clients retried, which amplified load.
[00:34] Ravi Kapoor: and to be clear, this was on our private deployment in eu-west-1 with customer-managed vault, right? not hosted?
[00:40] Jordan Hayes: correct, private deployment with Verdant-managed vault + our new fallback proxy. the fallback took longer than expected because of a TTL mismatch.

[00:55] Priya Nair: slide note, i'm paraphrasing logs — at 02:17 UTC the rotation job started, vault rotated keys but the vault-client had a 5m TTL and didnt refresh until 04:17 UTC, so the client attempted to use the old key for a period. some decrypt calls failed and triggered our fallback which tried to re-encrypt to proxy. that proxy endpoint had a brief capacity spike, leading to tokenization latencies.
[01:23] Elena Morales: so the mismatch was our TTL config plus rotation window — we didn't realize the client won't auto refresh mid-rotation?
[01:30] Priya Nair: yeah, it's a subtle interaction. the rotate job rotates and rotates metadata, but the client only checks at TTL expiry. Vault has multiple modes, and i think the client lib we shipped was using aggressive caching.
[01:43] Ben Chu: and for the record, some of the error messages in the logs were ambiguous — the stack said "decrypt failed" but it wasn't obvious it was key mismatch vs corrupted blob.

[02:01] Jordan Hayes: there's also an operational step: our fallback path re-encrypts with a hosted key which has different tokenization semantics. we should confirm no pii was exposed and that all writes were logged.
[02:12] Elena Morales: that's critical — SOC2 auditors will ask. we need a signed bundle of rotated keys audit and a list of request IDs that hit fallback.

[02:25] Priya Nair: actionably, we recommend: 1) short-term: revert the rotation for the smaller set while we patch the client TTL behavior, 2) widen CB (circuit-breaker) thresholds for the proxy, 3) export audit logs — which jordan will send, and 4) schedule a canary/dry-run in staging with HSM emulation.

[02:45] Ravi Kapoor: our question — why did the fallback hit the hosted proxy rather than a local cached key? we expected local in-memory cache to handle it.
[02:52] Priya Nair: the in-memory KV cache had evicted entries because of GC pressure — we saw memory churn around the same time due to another job. eviction+TTL mismatch equals no valid key locally.
[03:05] Sana Iqbal: uhh, can we confirm the eviction was due to our JVM flags? we bumped heap and saw spikes.
[03:12] Ben Chu: yeah, we changed -XX:MaxMetaspace and there was a permgen like effect, but the traces point to an OOM-ish GC pause.

[03:30] Jordan Hayes: ok realistic plan: immediate rollback of rotation for impacted keyset (we did this manually in the incident), but next steps are to instrument a canary rotation that uses a staged refresh step so clients refresh pre-rotation. that's priya's checklist.
[03:50] Priya Nair: i'll add automated client refresh in the client lib and publish a patch; we'll also provide a compat shim with toggles for rotation-window.
[04:02] Elena Morales: timeline expectation — auditors want documentation by next week. we need proof that the rollback didn't lose anything and the fallback didn't exfiltrate data.
[04:12] Marcus Lee: i'll assemble a compliance packet: signed audit export + list of fallback request ids + a short explainer. i'll hand it off to elena after jordan sends the raw exports.

[04:30] Ben Chu: and on capacity — the proxy had limited burst, which we should have foreseen. can we limit client retries to avoid thundering herd to the proxy?
[04:40] Priya Nair: yes, add jittered exponential backoff and a retry cap. also adaptive throttling on the proxy to shed non-critical traffic during rotations.

[05:01] Ravi Kapoor: longer term, we want HSM-backed rotations in staging, and to test rotation under load with the same heap settings as prod. can Redwood help provision ephemeral HSMs?
[05:10] Jordan Hayes: we can emulate HSM or do partner HSM in our dedicated infra. we'll propose both: emulation for quick tests, partner HSM for cert-level testing.

[05:25] Elena Morales: also, can you confirm RBAC for the fallback proxy logs? auditors will check who accessed keys.
[05:33] Priya Nair: yes, proxy logs contain actor identity (service principal). we'll include access control export and correlation ids.

[06:00] [interrupt] Sana Iqbal: quick nit — the client library name in logs was "redwood-priv" but in code it's redwood-private? little mismatch in naming in our internal docs so grep missed some traces.
[06:12] Priya Nair: ugh, sorry about that. that's on us — i'll normalize names in the runbook.

[06:28] Jordan Hayes: ok let's roleplay the postmortem timeline for the auditors — who did what and when. ben, can you recap?
[06:33] Ben Chu: at 02:17 rotate job starts, by 02:22 ~0.4% decrypts failing, 02:25 proxy accepts reroutes and starts spiking, 02:27 retries escalate load, by 02:40 ops notices elevated 5xxs, 02:50 rollback initiated and by 03:05 most traffic returned to normal. full recovery ~03:15.
[07:00] Elena Morales: that matches our internal timeline. we want the signed bundles and the runbook updates, and a plan for the canary.

[07:20] Jordan Hayes: agreed. next steps recap: jordan sends audit export + raw traces; priya publishes client lib patch and dry-run checklist; priya & rj (ravi) schedule the dry-run; marcus prepares compliance packet.

[07:43] Priya Nair: minor tech detail — we'll add a short-circuit in the client so if key-refresh fails it won't immediately go to proxy but will return a soft-failure that the caller can surface to the user gracefully. reduces proxy load.
[08:00] Ravi Kapoor: sounds good. one ask: can we have the dry-run simulate GC churn? we want to validate that eviction path is exercised.
[08:10] Priya Nair: yes we'll provide a stress script to create ephemeral GC pressure and observe behavior.

[08:24] Jordan Hayes: timeline for dry-run: target week of Jan 11-15. priya to pick exact date and share invite.
[08:32] Elena Morales: and auditors — we need the evidence by Jan 13 ideally.

[08:40] Ben Chu: i also want retros on instrumentation — add a specific metric for client key age and a histogram for time-since-last-refresh. that would've flagged this earlier.
[08:51] Priya Nair: noted, will add metrics and an alert threshold.

[09:05] [15 minute mark jump — summary handoff section]
[15:00] Marcus Lee: compliance packet items listed — signed key rotation audit (csv + GPG hash), fallback request id list, summary timeline, and mitigation plan. i'll assemble and run through internal QA before handing to elena.
[15:15] Elena Morales: thanks. on the packet, we might redact some PII before sending externally. we'll coordinate with Marcus.

[20:30] Jordan Hayes: bring up runbook handoff doc: https://redwood.example.com/docs/kms-rotation-runbook (note: link auto-captured, may require org access).
[20:40] Sana Iqbal: okay quick question — is the patch backward compatible with older client versions? we still have a small fleet on 1.2.
[20:47] Priya Nair: we'll publish the patch as opt-in toggle; full auto roll requires 1.3+. for older clients we'll ship a shim and a remediation guide.

[22:10] Ben Chu: any competitor notes — we looked at BigCompute's proxy approach but they require their hosted key, so not acceptable for us. good to know alternatives exist.

[23:05] Jordan Hayes: packaging notes: i'll send the raw exports to Marcus via the secure transfer and Marcus will produce the compliance bundle.

[24:00] [wrap-up]
[24:05] Jordan Hayes: final recap: immediate items sent by jan 6; dry-run scheduled by jan 13; patch in staging by jan 12; compliance bundle by jan 8. owners on action items in the chat follow.
[24:20] Elena Morales: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. this was helpful.
[24:30] Jordan Hayes: thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites and attachments.

-- End transcript --
